profile.reading:
This building on Beck Avenue in Fairfield, California is identified in local records as a Pacific Gas and Electric data center. PG&E is the investor owned utility serving electricity and natural gas to most of Northern and Central California, and Fairfield sits within its Solano County service territory roughly midway between the San Francisco Bay Area and Sacramento, a corridor where the utility maintains multiple operational facilities including service centers and grid support infrastructure.

Unlike the commercial and cloud operators that make up most of this registry, PG&E is not in the business of leasing data center capacity to outside customers. A utility owned data center of this kind almost certainly exists to run the company's own internal systems, including grid monitoring and control (SCADA and related operational technology), outage management, customer billing, asset and workforce management, and increasingly wildfire risk modeling and sensor data processing, which has become a major computing workload for California utilities following the wildfire liabilities of the past decade. Utilities generally treat this kind of infrastructure as critical to grid operations and, in some cases, as information that is protected from public disclosure under state and federal critical infrastructure security rules, which is a plausible reason detailed specifications are not published even though the building itself is a matter of public record through its address and ownership.

No power capacity, square footage, construction date or tenancy information specific to this Fairfield building has been found in PG&E's own public materials. That is consistent with how the company treats its operational facilities generally. PG&E publishes extensively about its generation assets, transmission and distribution infrastructure and wildfire mitigation programs, but does not maintain a public facing directory of its internal data centers the way a colocation or cloud company would for a marketed facility. Solano County property and permit records would be the most direct path to specifics such as parcel ownership, building square footage and year built, but no such record specific to this address has been reviewed for this entry. Absent that, the most that can be said with confidence is that this is very likely a utility owned and operated computing facility supporting PG&E's internal grid and business operations, rather than a commercial data center serving outside tenants, and that the company has chosen not to publicize its technical details.
